examples.title: Run a bounded MCP server as an owned stdio child
examples.assertion: A real child process completes initialize, catalog discovery, and one tool call over stdio. The transport supplies an explicit environment allowlist, owns shutdown, and never treats stderr as protocol data.
examples.cleanup: Client.Close drains the MCP session, closes the child's stdin, terminates the process group if needed, and reaps the child before the parent exits.

examples.title: Connect to an authenticated Streamable HTTP server
examples.assertion: A loopback server proves credentials are requested for each HTTP request, the negotiated session ID is reused, Client.Close releases the session with DELETE, and a 401 initialization failure is classified as auth_required without exposing the token. Tool calls are not retried; only an SSE read may resume with Last-Event-ID.
examples.cleanup: Client.Close releases the MCP session, then httptest.Server.Close stops the loopback listener. No remote service or credential is used.

examples.title: Author a tools-only MCP server behind the stable Looprig API
examples.assertion: A real in-memory MCP session proves tool registration, JSON argument decoding, text content, structured output, explicit server identity, bounded framing, and tools-only capability advertisement.
examples.cleanup: The SDK client session closes, the context is cancelled, and both ends of the in-memory pipe are released.

examples.title: Adopt MCP tools into a Harness loop at its boundary
examples.assertion: A required session-scoped binding starts through a real stdio child, an Adopter atomically installs a qualified mcp__docs__lookup definition for one loop, and DisableBinding retires the live connection. Sampling remains unadvertised because the binding does not request it; requesting sampling also requires a host SamplingPolicy and never grants tools or session authority to that policy.
examples.cleanup: Adopter.Close stops its subscription before Manager.Close retires routes and closes the owned stdio connection.

examples.title: Pass a collaboration request through the host-owned broker boundary
examples.assertion: A deterministic net.Pipe broker proves MessageAgent validation occurs before dialing, authenticates with a bounded binary capability, and returns only the public correlation-free result. MCP does not launch, proxy, or import ACP here; an ACP-capable host owns delegation and exposes only this narrow broker operation to its MCP process.
examples.cleanup: The collaboration client closes its one-request connection and the example closes the broker side of the in-memory pipe.
